title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that deployed an AI-generated fake website. The scam began with an unsolicited message directing them to a mobile trading app that appeared legitimate and showed real returns initially. After months of building confidence through small successful withdrawals, a final attempt to withdraw a large sum revealed the funds had never existed.

The failure occurred at the point of user verification. The scammers used an AI-generated fake website to display false investment balances and transaction history on the victim's screen, creating the illusion of legitimate trading activity. A human verification step, such as independently contacting the legitimate app through official channels or requiring verification from the app operator before large withdrawals, could have caught the deception before substantial funds were committed.

It is not established whether the app itself was compromised or whether scammers merely directed victims to open a real app while displaying false information through a separate AI-generated interface overlay. Authorities indicate recovery of funds in these cases is rare.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, and the couple initially saw modest returns and were able to withdraw funds, building their confidence. After months of trading with increasingly larger amounts, Jerry attempted a major withdrawal and discovered the funds were gone.

Investigators determined that while the app was real, scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that displayed false investment information on Jerry's screen. The couple is now working with Gwinnett County police, though authorities indicate victims in these cases rarely recover their money. The Dunaways are publicly warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers, and their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them with daily expenses.
